answer: Randomness-Gated Admission Windows. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon (threshold BLS) selects a small, unpredictable slice of the pending identity queue for admission, and only those selected may join. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will clear or when, so mass registration collapses into repeatedly paying full registration cost for mostly-rejected attempts. A sparrow-sized slice of honest applicants clears each round. The atlas of queued identities must be re-signed every epoch, and each attempt requires fresh randomness the glacier of prior outputs cannot predict,
